prose: An arXiv paper argues long context is less needed than assumed. Later tokens cost more to generate than early ones, up to 7x on open-weight frontier models. With frequent compaction, models lose little or no accuracy on long-horizon and long-input tasks, and do not collapse on software engineering even taking one action per context. The authors propose 'semantic state space models' and question the need for long-context models.
highlights: Late tokens can cost up to 7x more
Frequent compaction keeps accuracy on long tasks
Works even with one action per context
